September 3, 1932.

Honourable Solomon G. Arcus, suspected Soviet Agent

Information has been received to the effect that
one named Solomon Grigorievitch Arcus residing at No.681
Avenue Joffre, is a suspected Soviet Agent.

He is a Russian of Jewish origin. Prior to coming
to Shanghai some years ago, he resided in Harbin where
he owned a pharmacy in the Kartashevskaya Street. At
present he works as a representative of the "LALEV"
patent medicine preparation etc. and is connected in
this business with Arnhold & Co., Sassoon House.

He resides together with his sister Mrs. Arcus, widow
of his cousin, who was executed in Chita, Transbaikalian
Province, for communist activities in 1919. One of his
cousins holds the post of manager of the Soviet Government
Bank (GOSBANK) in Moscow.

Another cousin of his, C.H. Arcus is the proprietor
of the "Maison Arcus", No.212 Szechuen Road (Modes,
Military and Furs), (file I.O. 7561) and is known to be
an associate of E. Maharam, Soviet journalist and editor
of various Russian periodicals in Shanghai (file No. D. 320.)
Mr. Arcus brother, M.G. Arcus is employed at Lubbert's
Pharmacy, 81 Nanking Road.

（印：FILE 72 S.C./C.S.B）

G. Tcharnchansky.

尊敬的 Solomon G. Arcus，疑似苏联特工

收到情报称，一名名为 Solomon Grigorievitch Arcus、居住在霞飞路681号的人，是疑似苏联特工。

他是犹太裔俄罗斯人。在几年前来到上海之前，他居住在哈尔滨，并在卡尔塔舍夫斯卡亚街（Kartashevskaya Street）拥有一家药店。目前，他担任“LALEV”专利药品制剂等的代表，并在此业务上与沙逊大厦的阿诺德公司（Arnhold & Co.）有联系。

他与他的姐姐 Arcus 夫人同住，后者是他表亲的遗孀，其表亲因1919年在后贝加尔省赤塔从事共产主义活动而被处决。他的一个表亲担任莫斯科苏联政府银行（GOSBANK）经理一职。

他的另一个表亲 C.H. Arcus 是四川路212号“Maison Arcus”（时装、军需品和皮草）的业主（档案 I.O. 7561），众所周知其与 E. Maharam 有交往，Maharam 是苏联记者，也是上海各种俄文期刊的编辑（档案编号 D. 320。）Arcus 先生的兄弟 M.G. Arcus 受雇于南京路81号的 Lubbert 药店。

Date October 9, 1931.
Subject (in full) Arrival of Mr. and Mrs.C.H. Arcus from American.
Made by D.S. Makaroff. Forwarded by J.B.Km. D.I
With reference to the attached translation from French
Intelligence Report of October 5, 1931, inquiries show that Mr. and
Mrs.C.H. Arcus alias Linoff arrived in Shanghai from New York,
U.S.A. on October 2, 1931 by the s.s. "President Jackson".
According to our information the trip of Mr. and Mrs.
Arcus to U.S.A. was generally of a business nature, as Mrs. Arcus
has brought back with her a quantity of millinery and new designs
of the latest modes, for her establishment, known as "Maison Arcus",
Modes, Millinery and Furs, Ward Building, No.212 Szechuen Road.
During the absence of Mr. and Mrs. Arcus a certain
Mr.J.A. Patushinsky, accountant and assistant manager of the store
was in charge.
Upon their arrival here, they were met by Mr.E.
Maharam, a well known Soviet journalist and former editor of
various Russian periodicals in Shanghai. Mr.E. Maharam is an
old friend of C. Arcus, and Mrs.E. Maharam is connected with
Mrs. Arcus through her millinery establishment which she conducts
in her apartment at the China United Apartments No.104 Bubbling
Well Road.
D. S.
Officer i/c Special Branch.
Reg. Please file. The French
Intelligence Reports on communism filed se-
parately and not attached to regular
files.

REPORT ON C. H. Arcus.

Made by P. C. S. Ovsiannikoff Forwarded by

Mr. C. H. Arcus, Soviet citizen, illegal husband
alias Arcus
of Mrs. Linoff, living at 420 Yu Yuen Road and an old resident
of Shanghai, is the owner of a ladies dress-making saloon named
"Maison Arcus" at 212 Szechuen Road. He is a merchant by
profession, engaged in import of furs from Soviet Russia and
modes and millinery from Paris, France. He has had this business
for several years and his saloon is very well known among the
Foreign Community of Shanghai. Mrs. Linoff is the chief designer
of the Saloon and Arcus acts as manager. They employ four
Russian women, one man and several Chinese tailors. Mr. C. H.
Arcus visited Japan on several occasions in connection with his
business and on May 5, 1928 he again left for Japan by the s.s.
or U.S.A.
"President Taft" and probably he will visit Vladivostock in the
near future. He is well known among the Foreign Jewish Community
and it is quite possible that he is a member of M.D.P.R. and
makes a certain donation to this association, but so far there
is nothing known against him to show that he collects money
among the Foreign Jews for the benefit of the organization. The
attached is a report which refers to C.H. Arcus.

P. Ovsiannikoff

关于 C. H. Arcus 的报告。

由 P. C. S. Ovsiannikoff 制作 转呈者

C. H. Arcus 先生，苏联公民，Linoff 夫人的非法丈夫
（别名 Arcus），居住在愚园路420号，是上海的老居民，
拥有位于四川路212号的一家名为“Maison Arcus”的女装定制沙龙。
他的职业是商人，从事从苏联俄罗斯进口皮草以及从法国巴黎进口
时装和女帽的业务。他经营此业务已有数年，其沙龙在上海
外侨社区中颇有名气。Linoff 夫人是该沙龙的首席设计师，Arcus 担任经理。
他们雇佣了四名俄罗斯女性、一名男性和几名中国裁缝。C. H.
Arcus 先生因业务关系曾多次访问日本，并于1928年5月5日再次乘
“塔夫脱总统”号轮船或前往美国
离开前往日本，很可能他在不久的将来会访问符拉迪沃斯托克（海参崴）。
他在外籍犹太社区中广为人知，他很可能是 M.D.P.R. 的成员，
并向该协会提供一定的捐款，但截至目前，没有任何针对他的情况
表明他在外籍犹太人中间为该组织募集资金。附件是一份涉及 C.H. Arcus 的报告。

P. Ovsiannikoff

re Madame Linoff

Park Mansions 420 Yu Yuen Road are Chinese owned, Messrs Palmer
and Turner being the agents for the property, collect rents and

building and called on Mrs Grey in her flat. Mr. Grey was not
present. During the course of conversation with Mrs. Grey, she in-
formed him of all the noises she had heard during the past week.

tenants in the other flats had complained to him of unaccountable

butt to inspect his flat and to see for himself. This Mr. Gab-
butt did and Mr. Gabbutt informed me that Mr. Arcus' flat is most
luxuriously furnished and there is nothing there which could pro-
duce the sounds as alleged to be heard by Mr. & Mrs. Grey and
other tenants, except that Mrs. Arcus has an electric vacuum clea-

Made by Det. Supt. Reeves. Forwarded by

Sir,

I beg to report that on January 19th 1927, Mr. A.C. Grey
Detective Superintendent S.M.P., living in Flat 5 of the Green-
field Park Mansions, 220 Yu Yuen Road came to my house and gave
me the following information.

In the flat 4, immediately below his flat 5, lives Mr. & Mrs.
C.H. Arcus and for some days past Mr. Grey and also the persons
living on flat 3, have been disturbed during the night by the
constant running of what sounds to be an electric driven machine.
On January 18th 1927 the machine was running from 9:30 p.m. to
6 a.m. the next morning. It is not a sewing machine as it very
seldom stops, and it is my opinion that it is a small printing
press run by electricity obtained from the electric radiator
switch. As Mr. C.H. Arcus is a well known member of the Soviet
Community it is possible that a secret press has been installed
in his flat
therein. I visited Mr. Grey's flat on January 19th 1927 at 10 p.m.
but apparently the machine had ceased running for a time. Mr.
Grey stated the machine is apparently situated in Mr. Arcus'
bathroom as the noise is most pronounced beneath Mr. Grey's
bathroom, the flats being built alike.

Mr. Grey also informed me that there is at times considerable
hammering as if cases were being nailed down.

I am, Sir,
Your obedient servant,
Oscar A. Reeves
Det. Supt.

D. C. I.
